findings.reason: the section's own rule ("If the fleet's sessions and workers would exceed either limit, report blocked") will fire, and its remedy ("share one watch per node, if the change watch can be shared") is not reachable from the declared write paths, so the design or the verdict changes before dispatch.
findings.text: §49's second limit says "Each coordinator session runs its own MCP server, and each current-code child would hold a watch of its own", reads the 25 held instances as "one for each Claude session and worker process", and calls the instance count the scarce limit; but `_ProjectChangeWatch.__init__` calls `inotify_init1` once per tree (`reckon/change_streams.py:38`) and `_FleetChangeWatch` arms one such watch per mounted tree ("one tree at a time", `reckon/change_streams.py:241-243`) — with ~18 mounts in `~/.config/reckon/mounts.json`, one opted-in MCP process adds up to 18 instances, not 1, so against `max_user_instances` 128 on a node already holding 25 the headroom is about 5 processes, not about 100

findings.reason: the node will either fail its own gate or widen scope to memoise the directory identities, i.e. take on §46's path, and the plan never says which of the two the measure means.
findings.text: the first held bullet ("a second roadmap call inside the window makes no `stat` of a covered file, counted with a wrapper on `os.stat`") cannot be met by the declared mechanism: the memo returns early only in `_discovery_signature` (`reckon/serve.py:1208-1225`), so the walk's stats vanish, but `metadata_index._reuse_covered` still calls `covered_dir_identity` for every recorded directory on every call (`reckon/metadata_index.py:404`, docstring at 169-175) — a directory stat per covered directory per call, which §46 deliberately retained ("each covered path at most once per call"); the section's own Why lists `_reuse_covered`'s 7.44 s as part of the time it removes, and an unqualified `os.stat` wrapper will count those stats
